title: Transport of augmentations through a normalized comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal D_U,\mathcal D_V,\mathcal E_U,\mathcal E_V$ be categories [def-nagata-category]. All functors and natural transformations below use their ordinary categorical meaning: a natural transformation $a:S\Rightarrow T$ has components satisfying $T(t)a_X=a_YS(t)$ for every $t:X\to Y$. For $T=U,V$ let $\Delta_T,B_T:\mathcal D_T\to\mathcal E_T$, $L_T:\mathcal E_T\to\mathcal D_T$, $i_T:\Delta_T\Rightarrow B_T$, and natural isomorphisms $j_T:L_T\Delta_T\xrightarrow{\sim}1_{\mathcal D_T}$. Let $P:\mathcal D_U\to\mathcal D_V$ and $Q:\mathcal E_U\to\mathcal E_V$ be functors, with natural isomorphisms $\chi:\Delta_VP\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\Delta_U$ and $b:PL_U\xrightarrow{\sim}L_VQ$. Let $h:B_VP\Rightarrow QB_U$ be a natural transformation. Assume, for every $F\in\mathcal D_U$, the augmentation equation
$$h_F\circ i_{V,PF}=Q(i_{U,F})\circ\chi_F$$
and the constant-object normalization
$$b_{\Delta_UF}\circ P(j_{U,F}^{-1})=L_V(\chi_F)\circ j_{V,PF}^{-1}.$$
Set $C_T=L_TB_T$ and $\eta_{T,H}=L_T(i_{T,H})\circ j_{T,H}^{-1}$ for $H\in\mathcal D_T$, and define
$$\rho_F=b_{B_UF}^{-1}\circ L_V(h_F):C_V(PF)\to P(C_UF).$$
Then $\rho:C_VP\Rightarrow PC_U$ is natural, and for every $F$ one has both equalities
$$L_V(h_F)\circ\eta_{V,PF}=b_{B_UF}\circ P(\eta_{U,F}),\qquad \rho_F\circ\eta_{V,PF}=P(\eta_{U,F}).$$
Explicitly, for every $t:F\to F'$,
$$P(C_Ut)\circ\rho_F=\rho_{F'}\circ C_V(Pt).$$
No limit universal property, abelian or derived structure, or invertibility of $h$, $i_T$ or $\eta_T$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Fix $F\in\mathcal D_U$. All compositions below are well typed: $\eta_{V,PF}:PF\to L_VB_VPF$, $L_V(h_F):L_VB_VPF\to L_VQB_UF$, and $b_{B_UF}:PL_UB_UF\xrightarrow{\sim}L_VQB_UF$. Expanding $\eta_V$ and applying $L_V$ to the assumed augmentation equation gives
$$L_V(h_F)\circ\eta_{V,PF}=L_V(h_F\circ i_{V,PF})\circ j_{V,PF}^{-1}=L_V(Q(i_{U,F}))\circ L_V(\chi_F)\circ j_{V,PF}^{-1}.$$
This uses only preservation of composition by the given functor $L_V$ and associativity from [def-nagata-category].

proof.text:
The assumed constant-object normalization replaces the last two factors in Step 1:
$$L_V(h_F)\circ\eta_{V,PF}=L_V(Q(i_{U,F}))\circ b_{\Delta_UF}\circ P(j_{U,F}^{-1}).$$
Here both $L_V(\chi_F)\circ j_{V,PF}^{-1}$ and $b_{\Delta_UF}\circ P(j_{U,F}^{-1})$ have source $PF$ and target $L_VQ\Delta_UF$; this is direct substitution, with reassociation as in [def-nagata-category].

source.place: fix-lem-exchanges Proof Step 5, direct-image ingredient; agent expansion of the extracted normalized-augmentation transport calculation.

proof.text:
Apply the stated naturality condition of $b:PL_U\Rightarrow L_VQ$ to the morphism $i_{U,F}:\Delta_UF\to B_UF$. It says exactly
$$L_V(Q(i_{U,F}))\circ b_{\Delta_UF}=b_{B_UF}\circ P(L_U(i_{U,F})).$$
Substituting this into Step 2, reassociating by [def-nagata-category], and using preservation of composition by $P$, the result is
$$L_V(h_F)\circ\eta_{V,PF}=b_{B_UF}\circ P\bigl(L_U(i_{U,F})\circ j_{U,F}^{-1}\bigr)=b_{B_UF}\circ P(\eta_{U,F}).$$
This proves the first required equality directly from the hypotheses.

source.place: fix-lem-exchanges Proof Step 5, direct-image ingredient; agent expansion of the extracted normalized-augmentation transport calculation.

proof.text:
Compose the equality of Step 3 on the left with $b_{B_UF}^{-1}$. By the definition of $\rho$ and the inverse identity $b_{B_UF}^{-1}\circ b_{B_UF}=\mathrm{id}_{P(C_UF)}$, associativity and the identity law [def-nagata-category] give
$$\rho_F\circ\eta_{V,PF}=b_{B_UF}^{-1}\circ b_{B_UF}\circ P(\eta_{U,F})=P(\eta_{U,F}).$$
Only the stipulated invertibility of $b$ is used in this cancellation.

proof.text: The comparison is already constructed as the composite of the natural transformations Functor.whiskerRight h L_V and Functor.whiskerLeft B_U b.inv. Its component at F is L_V.map (h.app F) followed by b.inv.app (B_U.obj F), exactly the stated rho. Whiskering and composition use only functoriality, the given naturality of h and b.inv, and the category laws [def-nagata-category]. Thus the separate conjugation calculation of inverse naturality is supplied by the natural-isomorphism API.

source.place: fix-lem-exchanges Proof Step 5, direct-image ingredient; agent expansion of the extracted normalized-augmentation transport calculation.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.NatTrans.naturality to normalizedAugmentationComparison B_U L_V b h and t : F ⟶ F′. Its source map is L_V.map (B_V.map (P.map t)) and its target map is P.map (L_U.map (B_U.map t)). Symmetry gives exactly the displayed naturality equality for rho. This is the defining naturality condition, instantiated at the composite natural transformation of Step 5; no additional lemma or hypothesis is needed beyond [def-nagata-category] and the given categorical data.

No other group has split the item, it is not in the 2026-10-19 dropped list, and no re-split note applies because the item was created on 2026-10-22 and had no earlier proof. I checked all six steps by hand, tracking source and target of every map. Step 1 uses functoriality of L_V and the augmentation equation. Step 2 substitutes the normalization; both sides run from PF to L_V Q Δ_U F. Step 3 uses naturality of b at i_{U,F} and P-functoriality to get the first equality. Step 4 cancels b^{-1}b to get the second. Step 5 conjugates naturality of b at B_U t to get the inverse-naturality identity. Step 6 applies L_V to naturality of h and uses Step 5 to get naturality of rho. The proof uses every hypothesis and needs no hidden theorem, so the elementary marks are accurate. The only citation, def-nagata-category (Stacks 0014), supplies exactly the identity and associativity laws it is cited for. The parent lem-sf-cbc-direct-image-reduction-unit uses the item in Step 2 with the same orientation of b, j, chi and rho; it takes the normalization from clause (3) of lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization. Small cases: with all data identity the result reduces to h i_V = i_U. With b = -1 and chi = 1 the normalization fails, and without it rho eta = P(eta) would be false, so the hypothesis is needed. With b = chi = h = -1 the hypotheses hold and rho = 1. With i = h = 0 everything is 0, so non-invertible eta and h are allowed. Searches with LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle and grep are all recorded; the composite statement is not a one-line Mathlib specialization, so status split is correct. The source provenance is fix-lem-exchanges.proof.md Step 5, which I checked; proof_origin by=agent is correct, and no SGA is used. No fixes.
